<requirements_list>
  <requirement id="R1">
    <category>Existence</category>
    <description>DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope must expose the requestAnimationFrame(callback) method, which accepts a FrameRequestCallback argument and returns an unsigned long.</description>
    <spec_quote>interface mixin AnimationFrameProvider {
  unsigned long requestAnimationFrame(FrameRequestCallback callback);
  undefined cancelAnimationFrame(unsigned long handle);
};
Window includes AnimationFrameProvider;
DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope includes AnimationFrameProvider;</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R2">
    <category>Existence</category>
    <description>DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope must expose the cancelAnimationFrame(handle) method, which accepts an unsigned long handle argument and returns undefined.</description>
    <spec_quote>interface mixin AnimationFrameProvider {
  unsigned long requestAnimationFrame(FrameRequestCallback callback);
  undefined cancelAnimationFrame(unsigned long handle);
};
Window includes AnimationFrameProvider;
DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope includes AnimationFrameProvider;</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R3">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>A DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope must include the AnimationFrameProvider interface mixin, exposing the requestAnimationFrame() and cancelAnimationFrame() methods in dedicated workers.</description>
    <spec_quote>interface mixin AnimationFrameProvider {
  unsigned long requestAnimationFrame(FrameRequestCallback callback);
  undefined cancelAnimationFrame(unsigned long handle);
};
Window includes AnimationFrameProvider;
DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope includes AnimationFrameProvider;</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R4">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>A DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope must act as its own target object for animation frame state, maintaining its own map of animation frame callbacks and callback identifier independently of its owner Window or other workers.</description>
    <spec_quote>Each `AnimationFrameProvider` object also has a target object that stores the
provider's internal state. It is defined as follows:

If the `AnimationFrameProvider` is a `Window`
:   The `Window`'s associated
    `Document`

If the `AnimationFrameProvider` is a `DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope`
:   The `DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope`</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R5">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>A newly created DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope's animation frame callback identifier must initially be zero so that the first call to requestAnimationFrame() returns a handle of 1.</description>
    <spec_quote>an animation frame callback
identifier, which is a number that must initially be zero.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R6">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>A DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope whose owner set contains a Document object must be considered a supported AnimationFrameProvider, allowing requestAnimationFrame() and cancelAnimationFrame() to succeed.</description>
    <spec_quote>An `AnimationFrameProvider` provider is considered supported if any of the following are
true:

* provider is a `Window`.
* provider's owner set contains
  a `Document` object.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R7">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>A nested DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope whose owner set contains a supported DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope must be considered a supported AnimationFrameProvider, allowing requestAnimationFrame() and cancelAnimationFrame() to succeed.</description>
    <spec_quote>An `AnimationFrameProvider` provider is considered supported if any of the following are
true:

* provider is a `Window`.
* provider's owner set contains
  a `Document` object.
* Any of the `DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope` objects in provider's
  owner set are [supported](#concept-animationframeprovider-supported).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R8">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Invoking requestAnimationFrame(callback) in a supported dedicated worker must increment the worker's animation frame callback identifier by one and return the resulting unsigned long handle.</description>
    <spec_quote>3. Increment target's [animation frame callback identifier](#animation-frame-callback-identifier) by one,
   and let handle be the result.
4. Let callbacks be target's [map of animation frame
   callbacks](#list-of-animation-frame-callbacks).
5. Set callbacks[handle] to
   callback.
6. Return handle.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R9">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Invoking requestAnimationFrame(callback) in a supported dedicated worker must store callback in the worker's map of animation frame callbacks associated with the returned handle.</description>
    <spec_quote>4. Let callbacks be target's [map of animation frame
   callbacks](#list-of-animation-frame-callbacks).
5. Set callbacks[handle] to
   callback.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R10">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Invoking cancelAnimationFrame(handle) in a supported dedicated worker must remove the entry for handle from the worker's map of animation frame callbacks so that the cancelled callback is not invoked.</description>
    <spec_quote>2. Let callbacks be this's [target object](#concept-animationframeprovider-target-object)'s [map of
   animation frame callbacks](#list-of-animation-frame-callbacks).
3. Remove callbacks[handle].</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R11">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>Because a dedicated worker's map of animation frame callbacks is an ordered map, multiple callbacks registered via requestAnimationFrame() for the same animation frame must be invoked in the order in which they were registered.</description>
    <spec_quote>Each [target object](#concept-animationframeprovider-target-object) has a
map of animation frame callbacks, which is an
ordered map that must be initially empty</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R12">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When a callback registered with requestAnimationFrame() in a dedicated worker is invoked, it must be passed a DOMHighResTimeStamp time argument.</description>
    <spec_quote>callback FrameRequestCallback = undefined (DOMHighResTimeStamp time);</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R13">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When running animation frame callbacks for a dedicated worker with a timestamp now, all callbacks invoked during that animation frame turn must receive the same now timestamp argument.</description>
    <spec_quote>To run the animation frame callbacks for a [target object](#concept-animationframeprovider-target-object) target with
a timestamp now:

1. Let callbacks be target's [map of animation frame
   callbacks](#list-of-animation-frame-callbacks).
2. Let callbackHandles be the result of getting
   the keys of callbacks.
3. For each handle in
   callbackHandles, if handle exists in
   callbacks:

   1. Let callback be callbacks[handle].
   2. Remove
      callbacks[handle].
   3. Invoke callback with «
      now » and "`report`".</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R14">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When running animation frame callbacks in a dedicated worker, each callback must be removed from the map of animation frame callbacks before being invoked so that it executes only once unless rescheduled.</description>
    <spec_quote>1. Let callback be callbacks[handle].
   2. Remove
      callbacks[handle].
   3. Invoke callback with «
      now » and "`report`".</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R15">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When running animation frame callbacks in a dedicated worker, the callback handle keys must be snapshotted before iterating so that any callback registered via requestAnimationFrame() from within an executing callback is not invoked during the current frame turn and is deferred to a subsequent frame.</description>
    <spec_quote>2. Let callbackHandles be the result of getting
   the keys of callbacks.
3. For each handle in
   callbackHandles, if handle exists in
   callbacks:</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R16">
    <category>Common Use Cases</category>
    <description>When running animation frame callbacks in a dedicated worker, each snapshotted handle must be checked for existence in the callback map immediately before invocation, so that calling cancelAnimationFrame() for a later callback from inside an earlier callback in the same frame prevents the cancelled callback from being invoked.</description>
    <spec_quote>3. For each handle in
   callbackHandles, if handle exists in
   callbacks:

   1. Let callback be callbacks[handle].</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R17">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>Calling `requestAnimationFrame()` on a `DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope` that is not supported (i.e., its owner set does not contain a `Document` and contains no supported `DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope`) must throw a `"NotSupportedError"` `DOMException`.</description>
    <spec_quote>The `requestAnimationFrame(callback)`
method steps are:

1. If this is not [supported](#concept-animationframeprovider-supported), then throw a
   "`NotSupportedError`" `DOMException`.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R18">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>Calling `cancelAnimationFrame()` on a `DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope` that is not supported (i.e., its owner set does not contain a `Document` and contains no supported `DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope`) must throw a `"NotSupportedError"` `DOMException`.</description>
    <spec_quote>The `cancelAnimationFrame(handle)`
method steps are:

1. If this is not [supported](#concept-animationframeprovider-supported), then throw a
   "`NotSupportedError`" `DOMException`.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R19">
    <category>Error Scenarios</category>
    <description>When running animation frame callbacks in a worker, if a callback throws an exception, the exception must be handled with `"report"` behavior (reported to the worker global scope rather than propagating and aborting the execution of remaining scheduled callbacks).</description>
    <spec_quote>3. Invoke callback with «
      now » and "`report`".</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R20">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>When `cancelAnimationFrame(handle)` is invoked on a supported `DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope`, the entry for `handle` must be removed from the worker's map of animation frame callbacks so that the cancelled callback is not invoked.</description>
    <spec_quote>The `cancelAnimationFrame(handle)`
method steps are:

1. If this is not [supported](#concept-animationframeprovider-supported), then throw a
   "`NotSupportedError`" `DOMException`.
2. Let callbacks be this's [target object](#concept-animationframeprovider-target-object)'s [map of
   animation frame callbacks](#list-of-animation-frame-callbacks).
3. Remove callbacks[handle].</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R21">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>When running animation frame callbacks for a `DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope`, the keys of the map of animation frame callbacks must be snapshotted before iteration begins, so any new callback dynamically scheduled via `requestAnimationFrame()` during callback execution must not be invoked during the current animation frame run.</description>
    <spec_quote>To run the animation frame callbacks for a [target object](#concept-animationframeprovider-target-object) target with
a timestamp now:

1. Let callbacks be target's [map of animation frame
   callbacks](#list-of-animation-frame-callbacks).
2. Let callbackHandles be the result of getting
   the keys of callbacks.
3. For each handle in
   callbackHandles, if handle exists in
   callbacks:</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R22">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>When iterating over the snapshotted animation frame callback handles for a `DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope`, each handle must be checked to verify it still exists in the map of animation frame callbacks before invocation, so a callback dynamically cancelled via `cancelAnimationFrame()` by an earlier callback in the same frame must not be invoked.</description>
    <spec_quote>3. For each handle in
   callbackHandles, if handle exists in
   callbacks:

   1. Let callback be callbacks[handle].
   2. Remove
      callbacks[handle].
   3. Invoke callback with «
      now » and "`report`".</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R23">
    <category>Invalidation</category>
    <description>When running animation frame callbacks for a `DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope`, each callback's entry must be removed from the map of animation frame callbacks prior to invoking the callback, ensuring it is not re-invoked in subsequent animation frames.</description>
    <spec_quote>   1. Let callback be callbacks[handle].
   2. Remove
      callbacks[handle].
   3. Invoke callback with «
      now » and "`report`".</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R24">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope must include the AnimationFrameProvider interface mixin, exposing requestAnimationFrame() and cancelAnimationFrame() on dedicated worker global scopes.</description>
    <spec_quote>DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope includes AnimationFrameProvider;</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R25">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>A DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope whose worker owner set contains a Document object must be considered a supported AnimationFrameProvider.</description>
    <spec_quote>An `AnimationFrameProvider` provider is considered supported if any of the following are
true:

* provider is a `Window`.
* provider's owner set contains
  a `Document` object.</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R26">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>A DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope whose worker owner set contains a supported DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope (such as a nested dedicated worker owned by a Document-owned dedicated worker) must be considered a supported AnimationFrameProvider.</description>
    <spec_quote>An `AnimationFrameProvider` provider is considered supported if any of the following are
true:

* provider is a `Window`.
* provider's owner set contains
  a `Document` object.
* Any of the `DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope` objects in provider's
  owner set are [supported](#concept-animationframeprovider-supported).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R27">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>A DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope whose worker owner set contains neither a Document object nor any supported DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope (such as a dedicated worker owned by a SharedWorker) must not be considered a supported AnimationFrameProvider.</description>
    <spec_quote>An `AnimationFrameProvider` provider is considered supported if any of the following are
true:

* provider is a `Window`.
* provider's owner set contains
  a `Document` object.
* Any of the `DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope` objects in provider's
  owner set are [supported](#concept-animationframeprovider-supported).</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
  <requirement id="R28">
    <category>Integration</category>
    <description>When running animation frame callbacks in a worker, each callback must be invoked with the "report" exception behavior so that exceptions thrown by the callback are reported through the platform's exception reporting mechanism.</description>
    <spec_quote>Invoke callback with «
      now » and "`report`".</spec_quote>
  </requirement>
</requirements_list>
